extracted.intended_audience: attorneys admitted to state bars and practitioners before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff; disciplinary enforcement agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing USPTO reciprocal disciplinary proceedings under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including grounds for imposing exclusion, service and response requirements, interim limited recognition, publication/notice duties, and reinstatement obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director may impose reciprocal discipline (e.g., exclusion from practice before the Office) identical to discipline imposed by a state licensing authority pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24; the OED Director may file a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting such action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the state court has imposed discipline (here, disbarment by the Supreme Court of Illinois), the USPTO may request identical discipline unless the respondent establishes a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's obligation to file a response within 40 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall file, within 40 days, a response containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order directed the 40-day deadline; failure to file a timely response may result in a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact and imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice requirements for the Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was mailed by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the most current address listed by the state bar; USPS records indicating delivery constitute service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfying mailing requirements (first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the address reasonably believed to be where respondent receives mail) supports a finding that respondent received adequate notice (here, delivered December 22, 2010).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation declaration alternative (37 C.F.R. § 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may seek a brief extension to draft and file a resignation declaration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 as an alternative to contesting reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent requested a one-week extension to draft a resignation declaration but did not file such a declaration; filing under § 11.27 can be a procedural option to resolve the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of ethical misconduct triggering discipline (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a), 10.23(b)(5), 10.23(b)(6), 10.23(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations include conduct involving fraud, dishonesty, deceit, or misrepresentation; conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice; and conduct tending to defeat the administration of justice or bring the courts or legal profession into disrepute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order tied the USPTO exclusion to these C.F.R. provisions as further defined in 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5), based on the state-court findings that the respondent fraudulently over-billed clients and breached fiduciary duties (including violation of state professional conduct rules such as Rule 8.4 and Rule 1.5 for unreasonable fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of exclusion and limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the Office; respondent is not a registered patent practitioner and is not authorized to practice patent law before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order grants limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after that date for the sole purpose of facilitating compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: While excluded, respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 contains duties of excluded practitioners (e.g., notice to clients, transfer of files and matters); the limited 30-day recognition is solely to enable compliance with those obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificates; respondent shall not use or obtain any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This measure prevents the excluded individual from accessing or representing others in USPTO electronic systems until reinstatement; it is an affirmative obligation on the Office and a prohibition on the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and Official Gazette notice obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and shall publish a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion and its basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published notice summarizes the disciplinary findings and the basis (statutory and regulatory), and directs the public to the Reading Room where disciplinary decisions are posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures reciprocal and inter-jurisdictional awareness of the discipline imposed by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure compliance (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 sets the requirements and procedures for petitions for reinstatement after exclusion; full compliance is required for any reinstatement consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to governing statute and regulation establish the legal basis for the USPTO's reciprocal-discipline process and its remedies.
